evidence: app/src/app/pages/home/home.ts:26 — resource() drives the home page's entire dataset; stable only since v22 (2026-06)
app/src/app/pages/pokemon/pokemon-page.ts:29,40 — two chained resources power the Pokémon page, the app's richest route
app/src/app/app.config.ts:4-5 — otherwise long-stable providers only (provideBrowserGlobalErrorListeners, provideRouter)
reach.rationale: No experimental, preview or RC APIs; but every page's data loading rests on resource(), stabilized only ~5 months ago, plus the v22-only @Service decorator — squarely the 'recently-stable in central places' anchor.

evidence: app/src/app/core/poke-api.ts:52-173 — all HTTP, caching and data shaping funnel through one service; page components never touch fetch directly

app/src/app/pages/home/home-data.ts (via home.ts:26) and app/src/app/pages/pokemon/moves-data.ts (via pokemon-page.ts:40) — loader bodies live in plain functions outside the resource wrapper, easy to re-seat
app/src/app/pages/types-page.ts:27-29 — the resource() calls are uniform 3–5-line declarative blocks repeated across 6 files
containment.rationale: The newly-stable APIs appear in 6 files, so not perfectly contained, but usage is a single uniform pattern with all real logic behind PokeApi and plain loader functions; swapping the reactive wrapper would be mechanical.

evidence: app/src/app/pages/pokemon/pokemon-page.ts:40-46 — second resource keyed on params re-derives from selectedGame: derived reload-on-change is exactly what resource() buys over hand-rolled signal+effect
app/src/app/pages/home/home.ts:61-67 — effect/URL-sync pattern avoids loading flicker; nothing gratuitous
app/src/app/core/poke-api.ts:52 — @Service() is pure ergonomics over @Injectable({providedIn:'root'}); harmless but not capability a stable API lacked
justification.rationale: resource() genuinely earns its place (request-scoped async state, derived params, hasValue/error handling across every page); @Service is a marginal ergonomics choice. No novelty-for-novelty's-sake.

findings.issue: The app's central data-flow depends on resource(), which was experimental from v19–v21 and only stabilized in v22; if the team downgrades or lags an upgrade the API surface could drift
findings.suggestion: Fine as-is on v22; just keep the loader functions (home-data.ts, pokemon-data.ts, moves-data.ts) framework-free so the wrapper can be swapped, as already done

findings.issue: @angular/forms is declared as a dependency but the app uses no forms module (native form elements only)
findings.suggestion: Drop the unused dependency, or adopt the now-stable Signal Forms if form logic grows

summary: The app rides Angular's current v22 exactly: resource() signals and the new @Service decorator — both stabilized only in v22 (June 2026) — are used centrally, but nothing experimental, preview or flagged remains. All real data logic is isolated behind one PokeApi service and plain loader functions, so the newly-stable surface is cheap to swap. This is the low-risk end of forward-looking: idiomatic for where the framework is now, with essentially no breakage exposure.
